sentences.text: Colombian paleontologist María Páramo defined the new genus and species Yaguarasaurus columbianus based on an articulated skull, some vertebrae, and ribs.
The name Yaguarasaurus means "Yaguará lizard of Colombia".
The Yaguarasaurus discovered in Yaguará is now among the most complete materials known in South America.
An additional skull measuring 87 cm long implies that the animal could have been larger than the initial estimates.
Early fossils suggested a total length of approximately 5 meters based on a cranial length of 47 centimeters.
Remains were found in an Upper Turonian limestone bed of the La Frontera Formation near Yaguará, Huila, at a site called Cueva Rica.
Additional remains suggest even larger sizes, with one skull reaching a cranial length of 87 centimeters.
A 2023 hypothesis by Rivera-Sylva et al. classifies Yaguarasaurus as a basal member of the Plioplatecarpinae.
The species is classified within the subfamily Yaguarasaurinae.
Palci et al. (2013) created the subfamily Yaguarasaurinae, which is the sister group to Tethysaurinae.
An analysis by Makádi et al. (2012) grouped Yaguarasaurus with other primitive mosasaurs into the subfamily Tethysaurinae.
After the discovery of Pannoniasaurus, it became clear that Yaguarasaurus and other "russellosaurines" formed a clade of primitive amphibious mosasaurs related to the aigialosaurs.
Yaguarasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous (Turonian) period in Colombia, South America.
Yaguarasaurus lived approximately 90 million years ago during the Upper Cretaceous (Turonian) in Colombia.
The time range for Yaguarasaurus is the Turonian to Coniacian, from 93.9 to 85.7 million years ago.
